The Talmud (Bava Metzia 32b) teaches that one who has mercy on animals shares in the merit of the righteous. - Shelters often save lives, reducing suffering—an act of **hesed (kindness)**. 2. **Balancing Needs & Responsibility** - Judaism emphasizes **responsibility**—taking care of animals is a mitzvah (commandment) derived from Genesis 1:28 ("Be fruitful and multiply"). - If you can provide a loving home, adopting is a positive act. 3. **No Direct Prohibition** - There is **no explicit prohibition** in Jewish law against adopting pets, including cats. - Some modern rabbinic opinions encourage pet ownership as long as the animal is treated with kindness and proper care. ### **Conclusion:** Adopting a cat from a shelter is **halachically permissible and encouraged** as an act of kindness and responsibility.
